rules: Gospel passage coordinates are verified for presence in installed Douay, CPDV and Crampon research witness files, not against named printed editions.
One known range extension is Mark 4:35–41 (6 available numbered entries, through Mark 4:40); no synthetic 4:41. Printed witness collation required.
Synoptic parallels are only editorial candidate relationships and never silently merged. Different named Gospel persons are not resolved by speculation.
Parables have no historical incident pins; traditional sites and cities never certify exact scenes.
The order of Matthew 14 feeding before walking on the water is a source-derived review candidate, not a cross-Gospel identity adjudication.
No new Scripture prose, genealogies, events, artwork, coordinates, or publication approvals generated.

The Capernaum synagogue sentence occurs at John 6:60 in installed Douay/CPDV but at John 6:59 in installed Crampon; the original John 6:22-59 scene selection cannot claim one-to-one multilingual verse parity.

reviewedRows.title: The Baptism in the Jordan
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Matthew 3:13-17 locates the Baptism in the Jordan, but does not establish the precise bank or a modern baptismal site.

reviewedRows.title: The forty-day fast
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Matthew 4:1-11 says the wilderness and describes temptations without certifying a particular modern cliff, summit or monastery.

reviewedRows.title: Behold the Lamb of God
reviewedRows.existingLocationClaim: Jordan Valley · exact baptism site disputed
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: John 1:29-34 presents the Baptist's testimony, not a new event of baptism at a separate point. Do not duplicate Matthew's Baptism or attach the same precise site by inference.

reviewedRows.title: The first disciples follow Jesus
reviewedRows.existingLocationClaim: Jordan Valley · exact baptism site disputed
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: John 1:35-51 follows witness and disciples; a regional association with the Jordan does not locate every encounter, especially later Philip and Nathanael scenes.

reviewedRows.title: The wedding at Cana
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: John 2:1 identifies Cana of Galilee but does not authenticate any modern wedding church or archaeological Cana claimant.

reviewedRows.title: Jesus cleanses the Temple (John 2)
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: John 2:13-22 describes Jerusalem's Temple, but not a reconstructible surviving exact court coordinate. Keep John's narrated cleansing distinct from the Synoptic presentation pending parallel source adjudication.

reviewedRows.title: Nicodemus comes by night
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: John 3:1-21 does not name a house or city for the night encounter. Jerusalem comes from the preceding narrative setting (John 2:23), not the selected span.

reviewedRows.title: The Samaritan woman
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: John 4:5-6 names Sychar and Jacob's well; a modern pilgrimage site is a separate identification requiring archaeological and traditional evidence.

reviewedRows.title: The royal official’s son is healed
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: John 4:46 names Cana as the location of the request and Capernaum as the location of the sick child. Do not collapse the dialogue and remote healing into one Capernaum point.

reviewedRows.title: Capernaum, the synagogue
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Mark 1:21 names Capernaum and a synagogue but does not identify an excavated synagogue building as the exact first-century interior.

reviewedRows.title: Peter’s mother-in-law healed
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Mark 1:29 identifies the house of Simon and Andrew immediately after the synagogue event; a particular modern house reconstruction remains interpretive.

reviewedRows.title: A paralytic lowered through the roof
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Mark 2:1 places Jesus at Capernaum; the roof and house cannot be assigned to an excavated room or distinct modern dwelling.

reviewedRows.title: The centurion’s faith
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Matthew 8:5 places the centurion's approach at Capernaum; Luke 7:1-10 is a distinct witness with different narrative intermediaries. Do not create fabricated merged dialogue.

reviewedRows.title: Levi leaves the tax booth
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Mark 2:13-17 describes the lakeside tax booth and a meal, without certifying an identifiable building or proving identity links across Gospel naming by location alone.

reviewedRows.title: The call of the fishermen
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Luke 5:1 names the lake of Gennesaret and a particular catch; no precise boat position or shore segment is established. Distinguish Luke's narrated call from Mark 1:16-20 unless editorially compared.

reviewedRows.title: The Twelve are chosen
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Luke 6:12 describes a mountain without naming which one or a settlement. Apostle identities in the source list need canonical-person review independently.

reviewedRows.title: The Sermon on the Mount
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Matthew 5:1-12 says mountain, not a named modern hill. A Mount of Beatitudes church site is traditional rather than an event coordinate.

reviewedRows.title: The Lord’s Prayer
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Matthew 6:5-15 belongs to the Sermon context; a repeated Lord's Prayer scene must not be presented as a second invented geographical occasion. Luke 11's prayer has a distinct Gospel setting.

reviewedRows.title: The widow’s son at Nain
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Luke 7:11-17 names Nain and its gate, but no exact surviving ancient gate or funeral location is established.

reviewedRows.title: The sinful woman anoints his feet
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Luke 7:36-50 does not give a town or name the woman. Do not identify her as Mary Magdalene, Mary of Bethany or John 12's anointer without separately attested interpretation.

reviewedRows.title: The parable of the sower
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Mark 4:1-20 has lake and boat context, but the sower's field is parabolic, not a surveyed historical farm.

reviewedRows.title: The storm is calmed
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: The imported three Catholic source transcriptions each number Mark 4 only through verse 40 and include the disciples' question in verse 40; scene's Mark 4:35-41 reference exceeds those imports. A printed-edition boundary collation is required; do not invent verse 41.

reviewedRows.title: The Gerasene demoniac
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Mark 5:1 locates the event in the country of the Gerasens in the installed Douay witness. Gerasene/Gadarene and modern eastern-shore site identification require synoptic/edition review.

reviewedRows.title: Jairus’s daughter raised
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Mark 5:21-43 spans a crowd and a house, and intercalates the haemorrhaging woman's healing. The scene should not collapse two encounters or assert a Capernaum house address absent in the span.

reviewedRows.title: The Twelve sent to preach
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Matthew 10:1-15 commissions the Twelve and gives directions for unnamed destinations; it is not a geocodable continuous tour.

reviewedRows.title: The beheading of John the Baptist
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Mark 6:17-29 describes imprisonment and execution but names no fortress. Machaerus is a later historical association requiring explicit external witness and cannot be a Bible-text coordinate.

reviewedRows.title: Jesus walks upon the water
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Matthew 14:22-33 follows Matthew 14:13-21 (feeding five thousand); the current source list places this walking-on-water scene before scene 096 loaves. Flag editorial order for review, not a premature cross-Gospel identity join.

reviewedRows.title: The multiplication of loaves
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: John 6:1-15 identifies the Galilean sea setting but not Tabgha as the actual multiplication site; traditional shore association must not become a precise event coordinate.

reviewedRows.title: The Bread of Life discourse
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: John 6:22–59 is the Bread of Life discourse span, but the location statement about teaching in the Capernaum synagogue falls at John 6:60 in the installed Douay and CPDV witnesses, versus John 6:59 in Crampon. Do not silently align the 59th verse across editions or certify a first-century synagogue structure.

reviewedRows.title: The Syrophoenician woman
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Mark 7:24-30 places the episode in the territory of Tyre, not a certified city house or excavated location. Preserve the unnamed daughter's separate identity.

reviewedRows.title: The deaf man healed
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Mark 7:31-37 takes place after travel by Sidon toward the Sea of Galilee through Decapolis; no exact lakefront site is named.

reviewedRows.title: The feeding of four thousand
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Matthew 15:32-39 records feeding four thousand, distinct in Matthew from the earlier five thousand; do not merge scene 100 with 096, regardless of shared bread imagery.

reviewedRows.title: The blind man of Bethsaida
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Mark 8:22 names Bethsaida and places the healing outside the village. Modern candidate sites compete, and the precise healing place is not established.

reviewedRows.title: Peter’s confession
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Matthew 16:13 says the district/quarters of Caesarea Philippi, not an exact cave or grotto for Peter's confession. Banias is a regional modern correspondence only.

reviewedRows.title: First prediction of the Passion
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Matthew 16:21-28 follows the confession but does not repeat Caesarea Philippi; do not invent a new location or depict the Passion prediction as the Passion event itself.

reviewedRows.title: The Transfiguration
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Matthew 17:1-9 says a high mountain but does not name Tabor. The map may show traditional Tabor with explicit status, not an authenticated biblical coordinate.

reviewedRows.title: The possessed boy healed
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Mark 9:14-29 follows descent from the mountain but does not name a town or identify a modern site.

reviewedRows.title: The man born blind at Siloam
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: John 9:1-12 names the pool of Siloam where the man washed, not the exact place Jesus first encountered or an incontrovertible excavated point for the entire healing.

reviewedRows.title: The Good Shepherd
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: John 10:1-21 records a figure of speech/discourse without naming Jerusalem in the selected passage; verse 22 begins a different festival setting. No sheepfold field or specific address exists to map.

reviewedRows.title: The Good Samaritan
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Luke 10:25-37 gives the Jerusalem-to-Jericho road as the setting inside a parable, not the actual location of a documented injured traveller.

reviewedRows.title: Martha and Mary
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Luke 10:38 describes an unnamed village and Martha's house. Bethany is supplied by other tradition/Gospel material, not by Luke's selected text.

reviewedRows.title: The prodigal son
provisionalActorsForSourceReview: father and two sons within parable
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Luke 15:11-32 is a parable without a historically identifiable town, father, vineyard, pigs' field or biographical persons.

reviewedRows.title: Ten lepers cleansed
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Luke 17:11 places the journey between Samaria and Galilee and 17:12 an unnamed village, not a specific town or leper station.

reviewedRows.title: Zacchaeus of Jericho
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: Luke 19:1 names Jericho, but the particular sycamore tree or house is not authenticated by Luke 19:1-10.

reviewedRows.title: Lazarus is raised
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: John 11:1 names Bethany as Lazarus' village. The cave/tomb visited today is a traditional identification, not independently proved from the passage; preserve the plot leading to resurrection.

reviewedRows.title: The anointing at Bethany
reviewedRows.editorialFinding: John 12:1-8 explicitly names Bethany and Mary the sister of Lazarus; distinguish this from Luke 7's unnamed woman and other Gospel anointing accounts until independently adjudicated.
